Known-good QA fixture

Activity practice · about 14 min
Objectives
  • Complete a safe interaction and explain why it is safe.
  1. Activity 1
  2. Activity 2
  3. Activity 3

Teaching

A local effect stays within this page. An external effect crosses a system boundary to contact something else. Complete work stays in place when you revisit an activity.

Another way to think about itOptional example

A café worker can update the chalkboard beside them, but changing a supplier delivery means contacting another business.

A local action stays in one workspace; an external action crosses a system boundary.

Where this fits

Decision: Decide whether an effect should stay on this page or cross a boundary.

Good fit: Use the local control for a bounded, self-contained practice change.

Choose something else when: The work must contact another system or coordinate several dependent steps.

Activity 1 — Your task: classify an effect

A note preview appears only in this practice page. Choose where that effect stays, then check your choice.

Where does the preview effect stay?

What success looks like

You classify the in-page preview as local and keep your observation when you revisit.

0 of 1

Challenge (optional)

Optional time: about 2 minutes

Success criteria: Describe one local effect and one effect that crosses a system boundary.

Activity 2 — Your task: explain your choice

Explain in the field below why your first action stays local.

Need a hint?Hint 1 of 2 for Activity 2

Where to act: Start in the explanation field above the boundary checkbox.

Next step: Name the boundary your chosen effect does not cross.

Another hintAnother hint, 2 of 2 for Activity 2

Where to act: Compare the Effect scope choice with your explanation.

Next step: Use the observed result location as evidence that both choices describe the same boundary.

Activity checks

Your explanation and scope choice both identify why the preview stays local.

Back to activity 1

Activity 3 — Your task: recap

Review your saved note and explanation, then state the boundary.

What success looks like

Your recap distinguishes the local preview from an effect that contacts another system.

Back to activity 2

Recap

Choose a local effect when work stays in the current workspace; choose an external approach when it must cross a system boundary.

Printed alternative: choose a local control, then explain the observed in-page result.
